liveDemonstration1.requestedPairs: 48491 x {wells, specialDistricts, valueHistory} in one --apply run
liveDemonstration1.action: Real external kill via `gcloud run jobs executions cancel factory-publish-gate-sched-ft929` (not a mocked in-process throw) after the execution ran unusually long (~11 minutes) under heavy store write contention from the concurrent fill-ownership heal pass.
liveDemonstration1.outcome: Two of three pairs had already completed and their verdicts stand untouched (48491/wells=pass, 48491/specialDistricts=pass, both confirmed present post-kill). The third (valueHistory) was never attempted -- zero rows in parcel_gate_verdict for that pair, confirmed by direct query -- which is the exact 'missing verdict from an interrupted run, indistinguishable from not-evaluated-yet' case the mission names.
liveDemonstration1.runRowFinding: GENUINE, NEWLY-DISCOVERED GAP: an external Cloud Run cancel (SIGTERM/SIGKILL from infrastructure) does not give runPublishGateSched's own catch block a chance to run, so writeTermination is never called by the process itself -- the run row was left status='running' indefinitely, the same shape as the already-known 122cd0b2 phantom-run issue (flood-fragments card, a different job). This is a real repro of that same class of gap on publish-gate-sched specifically, not previously confirmed for this job.
liveDemonstration1.resolution: Corrected via the sanctioned path named for exactly this situation: `gcloud run jobs execute factory-conformant --args=reap,terminate,--run=750f6cc4...,--exit-kind=cancelled,--reason=<real evidence>,--execution=factory-publish-gate-sched-ft929,--apply`. Verified: runs.status now 'cancelled' (was 'running'), termination_records row present (exit_kind=cancelled, recorded_at 2026-09-02T21:58:32.425Z). Never hand-wrote to the store from a laptop; used the existing Cloud Run mechanism built for this exact case.

refuseCase.unitLevelCoverage: toGateVerdictKind is exercised directly by three unit tests (mapping ok:true/no-exclusion -> 'pass', ok:false -> 'refuse', excludedDeclaredAhead non-empty -> 'excluded' even when ok:true, a falsifier), and the full write path's kill-mid-run test independently re-confirms 'refuse' is what gets written and stored for an unaccounted-carrying rail (fakeVerdictPayload with ok:false, unaccountedCount:3, asserted as row.verdict==='refuse' post-write). All green in CI on the merged commit.
refuseCase.honestAssessment: The REFUSE branch of toGateVerdictKind is the SAME function, same code path, same UPSERT_VERDICT_SQL statement that already fired correctly for 'excluded' and 'pass' live in production this session -- there is no code-path reason to expect 'refuse' behaves differently, and it is unit-verified with a real assertion, not merely asserted. Declaring this explicitly rather than silently treating unit coverage as equivalent to a live production instance: this is a genuine gap in live-instance coverage specifically for the REFUSE enum value, caused by store contention outside this card's control, not by any defect found in the mechanism.

constraintsHonored: store writes only via Cloud Run jobs with run rows: every evaluation, both cancels' corrections, and the migration all ran via gcloud run jobs execute against digest-pinned images -- zero laptop applies

state-changing operations left a durable record naming what was acted on: both manual reap-terminate calls carried real, specific evidence (execution name, cancellation timestamp, which pairs completed) in --reason, never a generic string
did not fabricate or guess an exit kind for either stuck run -- both were externally verified via gcloud describe ("Cancelled by user") before the reap terminate call
no unaccounted cell converted to absent-verified or any other state -- this card only reads parcel_record_cell and writes parcel_gate_verdict/runs/termination_records

at most one other parcel_record writer concurrent: PARCEL-FILL-OWNERSHIP (a peer-held card, read-visible via its heal pass's live effects on Williamson) was the only other writer observed; this card's own writes never touched parcel_record_cell

LESSON: An external `gcloud run jobs executions cancel` sends a real kill signal that bypasses a Node process's own try/catch termination-recording logic -- only an in-process thrown error (as unit tests simulate) reaches that catch block. A live kill test therefore needs its own explicit reap-terminate follow-up; it does not self-heal the way the unit test's mocked kill does.

Two live cancels both correctly demonstrated fails-closed via a genuinely empty result set for the untouched pair, which is the property that actually matters to the allowlist -- the run row's own bookkeeping status is a separate, secondary concern from what the allowlist reads.

Chasing one specific live enum value (REFUSE) against a large, actively-being-healed county under heavy concurrent writer contention has a real time cost that can exceed its marginal verification value once the code path is already proven correct for the other two enum values through the identical function and write statement.
